behavior: Blocking required stdout pipes poll at most 100 ms and write no more than runtime PIPE_BUF, with cancellation around every wait/write. Native writes elsewhere are capped at INT_MAX; nonblocking EAGAIN fails immediately.

Required-delivery cancellation latches status 130 and suppresses subsequent stdout records; delivery failure latches status 1. A provider cancellation may still emit its existing secondary failure event to an immediately writable destination without waiting.

Private duplicated terminal streams detach to a reserved sink before background or unknown-ownership cleanup. Final cleanup preserves foreground modes and input, native release order, and masks. ENOTTY PTYs retain existing restoration behavior.

Human rendering normalizes CRLF, escapes lone CR and the unchanged unsafe set, and stops on complete characters or escape tokens. Exhausted ordinary budgets skip input work. Trusted rendered paths avoid repeated encoding.
TTY text exports render through the 64 KiB staging buffer; redirected, structured and file payloads remain raw. Redirected answers borrow their existing storage.
Raw fd-2 and injected stream separators have separate fixed owners, rebound by descriptor identity or rdbuf and reset per invocation. Emergency delivery remains best effort without EAGAIN waiting.
Bounded stack writev gathering combines spans/newlines; scalar paths remain for single spans. Short vectors, cancellation, limits, no replay and original exceptions remain covered.

initial_validation_notes: The initial full Debug run exposed suppressed cancellation failure events. The reporting path was corrected to preserve the existing turn.failed event only when output is already writable; the original regression remains unchanged.

A later ASan run failed the unchanged Followup.OneShotExitSurvivesSignalAndReapFailures test with Child process setup failed. Thirty isolated repetitions passed, then the final full suite passed. No root cause or baseline reproduction is claimed.

One CLI repetition timed out waiting for the background cleanup helper readiness token in line mode. The PTY supervisor now closes unused gate ends, retains startup diagnostics, and detects early child exits/stops instead of reporting a blind timeout; the root cause remains unproven and original failure evidence is retained.

A subsequent repetition exposed a parent setpgid/child exec race in the active job-control supervisor. Parent setup now accepts PermissionError only after getpgid verifies the child already owns the expected process group. This changes fixture setup, not the job-control assertions or production code.

Initial PTY fixture assertions mixed integer and byte control characters and compared against libedit-mutated newline settings. The fixture now compares the kernel-normalized foreground settings and queued input at a deterministic handoff gate.

New Cppcheck initialization/parameter findings and Clang-Tidy noexcept/assignment findings were fixed without suppressions. An initial Cppcheck attempt overlapped offline dependency replacement; its incomplete-header result was discarded and the complete final run was isolated from provisioning.
The new redirected-answer allocation test initially missed its cli_output.hpp include. Both focused tests and the complete suites passed after adding it.
Unconditional vector gathering was removed from single-span output after measurements showed unnecessary work. Final gathering retains the scalar paths for single spans and single-vector batches.

performance.procedure: Two sets, each one warm-up and five alternating measured runs, identical harnesses/compiler flags. No concurrent analyzers, tests or builds. Pipe drainer and loopback HTTP fixture are intrinsic benchmark helpers.
notes: Whole-change blocking-pipe timing includes additional readiness operations and runtime PIPE_BUF chunking. Darwin PIPE_BUF is 512 bytes, causing a substantial throughput cost; these operations provide bounded cancellation checks. No throughput improvement is claimed for blocking pipes.

The deterministic answer-boundary case and allocation-fault/pointer-identity regression establish removal of the redirected answer copy. Full HTTP answer allocation totals vary with curl chunking and reallocation; they are contextual end-to-end measurements, not copy-removal proof.

Regular-file and /dev/null exports measure complete CLI execution including SQLite loading. Isolated scalar/gathering controls hold correctness policy constant. No general export latency improvement is claimed.

Write counters intercept native write/writev calls; readiness counts intercept poll. Stream flush observations are distinct. Allocations and byte counts cover measured C++ new operations, not all C library allocations.

Isolated small regular-file export medians increased by 0.85% and 0.15%; paired samples have mixed directions (paired median changes approximately +0.02% and -1.06%) and overlapping spreads. Large regular-file medians decreased in both sets. This is treated as measurement noise rather than a repeatable file-export slowdown; all raw samples and unchanged operation/allocation counts are published.
No timing-based CI threshold is added.

ascii_assembly_inspection: O2 ASCII repair/path branches bypass decoder; decoder is inlined in O2.
O3 decoder calls remain only on non-ASCII repair/path branches.

limitations: Local validation is macOS arm64 with Apple Clang 21.0.0. Linux and native Tiger runtime acceptance were not executed locally.
Existing local build warning exceptions are -Wno-error=implicit-int-float-conversion and -Wno-error=unused-result, unchanged from the baseline builds.

Clang-Tidy 18.1.8 uses the existing SDK13 wrapper; one translation unit remains incomplete and six recorded-main findings remain. Clang Analyzer reports the same existing context.cpp division-by-zero finding. Those analysis gates are not clean; no checks or suppressions were weakened.
The legacy default benchmark has the previously recorded Glob failure and is not used for a new performance claim.
Descriptor readiness cannot reserve pipe capacity against unrelated competing writers. No descriptor flags or global stdio buffering are changed.
Emergency descriptor output is one best-effort attempt; it does not wait for EAGAIN or guarantee delivery. Partial output duplicates and conservative separators remain accepted.
